description: issue #775 (review gate, QA finding B1): `every "2.5"` -- a WORD that parses as a number but not a whole one. This is the third arm of `every`'s `ol-type` tick-count check, the twin of `wait/wait-non-whole-word`, sitting between `every-non-whole-type-error` (the number `2.5`) and `every-non-number-type-error` (the word `"soon"`, which does not parse as a number at all). It is the arm that pins WHICH value the diagnostic names: `spec/execution-model.md:33-34` makes "words that parse as numbers are accepted where a number is expected" a normative CORE rule, so the word is coerced far enough to be judged non-whole -- but the value the learner actually wrote is a word, so `params.actual` is `word` and `params.value` is the string `"2.5"`, NOT `number`/`2.5`. Without this fixture an implementation could pre-coerce the word before the wholeness check -- exactly the defect #775 removed from `wait` -- and still pass the whole corpus, because the other two arms never observe the difference (a number literal was never a word, and a non-numeric word never coerces at all). That gap was found by mutation: reintroducing the pre-coercion on `every` survived a fully green run. As with every other failed `every` validation the check fails BEFORE registration, so no `primitive` event is emitted and no handler is registered; only the registration `instruction` precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the count argument.
